The learner leads by 1.04–1.14 in L2a (split-cluster CI lower bounds 1.043–1.089) and by 1.06–1.13 in L6a, with intervals excluding 1. The edge is conditional, since it reverses at 10% budget and on E01, but the confound is controlled, so W2 is false. Claim 3: E04 is a different proxy (answer-only judge, 3B and 7B). Its embedding AUC gain is −0.0003 to −0.003 and its neighbor ratio is 1.00. L1a repeats the null (gain below 0.01). The ledger holds claim 3 dead, so W3 is false.

Claim 2: L2a, L6a and L7b compare the learner with fixed rules at matched budget. Calibration labels are charged and counted, so the fixed rule has no information advantage. Learner/fixed ratios are 1.05–1.14 (L2a), 1.06–1.13 (L6a) and 1.07–1.14 (L7b), with CIs above 1. The free-label rules (L12c) are excluded as having an information advantage. The edge is conditional (it reverses at small budgets), but the charged-baseline confound is controlled, so W2 is false. Claim 3: E04 (judge proxy, different from E01) shows delta AUC −0.0003 to −0.003 and neighbor ratio 1.00. L1a shows PC delta +0.0097, below 0.05. Both are under the thresholds, so claim 3 is killed. The ledger holds it unsupported, so W3 is false.

Claim 2: L2a and L6a/L7b compare the learner to fixed rules whose calibration labels are charged to the same budget (no free labels). Ratios 1.05–1.14 with CIs excluding 1. This controls the free-label confound. The L12c free-label rules have an information advantage, so they don't count. Claim 3: E04 uses a different proxy (judge) and gives embedding delta AUC −0.0003 with neighbor ratio 1.00. L1a gives PC delta +0.008–0.010. Both are below the thresholds, so the claim is killed. W2 is false because the confound was controlled. W3 is false because no entry asserts claim 3 is supported.
